items.title: Atlantic Nickel produz recorde de 12,5 mil t de concentrado de níquel na Bahia em agosto
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: A mineradora Atlantic Nickel, controlada pelo fundo de private equity britânico Appian Capital, atingiu um recorde mensal de produção em agosto de 12.464 toneladas de concentrado de níquel, informou a companhia nesta terça-feira à Reuters.
items.body:
A mineradora Atlantic Nickel, controlada pelo fundo de private equity britânico Appian Capital, atingiu um recorde mensal de produção em agosto de 12.464 toneladas de concentrado de níquel, informou a companhia nesta terça-feira à Reuters.
O volume produzido na Mina Santa Rita, em Itagibá (BA), cresceu 17,4% ante o mesmo mês do ano passado, apagando o recorde anterior de 12.113 toneladas, em dezembro de 2024.
Do total, o percentual do metal aproveitado a partir do minério somou 86,72%, afirmou a empresa.
"São os melhores números desde 2019, quando o grupo assumiu as atividades. O resultado confirma a consistência da operação e o avanço da estratégia de crescimento", disse a companhia, em um comunicado.
A produção de concentrado no primeiro semestre de 2026 totalizou 61.995 toneladas, crescimento de 4,3% na comparação anual.
A alta na produção veio acompanhada de um avanço mais expressivo na receita. No primeiro semestre de 2026, a receita bruta alcançou R$833 milhões, alta de 33% ante o mesmo período do ano anterior.
"Alcançamos recordes importantes ao mesmo tempo em que seguimos preparando a Mina Santa Rita para sua próxima etapa de crescimento, mantendo os mais elevados padrões de segurança e sustentabilidade", disse o country manager da Appian Capital Brazil, Milson Mundim.
De janeiro a junho, a Atlantic Nickel registrou Ebitda ajustado de R$339 milhões e lucro líquido de R$293 milhões.
O custo caixa C1 ficou em US$3,10 por libra de níquel. Esse indicador mede os custos diretos de produção e mostra a competitividade da mina no mercado global.

items.title: China planea sumarse a la carrera por el liderazgo de la OMS, dicen fuentes
items.author: Emma Farge, Olivia Le Poidevin, Stanley Widianto
items.creator: Emma Farge, Olivia Le Poidevin, Stanley Widianto
items.summary: China tiene previsto presentar un candidato de última hora para dirigir la Organización Mundial de la Salud (OMS), según cuatro diplomáticos y una fuente familiarizada con el asunto, lo que brinda a Pekín la oportunidad de ampliar su influencia tras la salida de Estados Unidos de la agencia.
items.body:
China tiene previsto presentar un candidato de última hora para dirigir la Organización Mundial de la Salud (OMS), según cuatro diplomáticos y una fuente familiarizada con el asunto, lo que brinda a Pekín la oportunidad de ampliar su influencia tras la salida de Estados Unidos de la agencia.
Pekín lleva tiempo tratando de asumir más responsabilidades en los organismos de la ONU y otras instituciones multilaterales, justo cuando Estados Unidos, bajo el mandato del presidente Donald Trump, reduce su participación en la ONU y en algunas de las organizaciones que la constituyen.
La OMS lidera los esfuerzos internacionales para combatir enfermedades y crisis sanitarias, como el actual brote de ébola en la República Democrática del Congo y la reciente pandemia de COVID-19.
Las fuentes indicaron que China tiene previsto presentar la candidatura de Song Li, una alta funcionaria de salud pública con 20 años de experiencia en políticas de salud materno-infantil y cooperación internacional, para suceder al actual director general, Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus.
Ni Song ni la misión china en Ginebra respondieron de inmediato a las solicitudes de comentarios de Reuters.
Una fuente diplomática señaló que la candidatura prevista era una clara señal de que China quería llenar el vacío que ha dejado Estados Unidos al dar un paso atrás.
La agencia de salud de la ONU se ha visto obligada a llevar a cabo una reestructuración radical tras la pérdida de su mayor donante, lo que ha supuesto la reducción de actividades, el recorte de puestos de alta dirección y la eliminación de miles de puestos de trabajo.
El Gobierno del presidnete estadounidense Donald Trump criticó en repetidas ocasiones la gestión de la pandemia por parte de la OMS y la acusó de parcialidad hacia China, lugar donde se originó la COVID-19, algo que la OMS rechaza.
China ha anunciado una financiación adicional para la OMS, pero está lejos de cubrir el vacío dejado por Estados Unidos.
La OMS publicará la lista completa de candidatos tras las reuniones finales de los comités regionales, previstas para principios de noviembre.

items.title: GRANOS Maíz sube ante preocupación por rendimientos en EEUU tras reporte USDA sobre estado cosechas
items.author: Karl Plume
items.creator: Karl Plume
items.summary: Los futuros del maíz estadounidense se dispararon el martes después de que el Departamento de Agricultura anunciara un recorte mayor de lo esperado en su valoración del estado de la cosecha, lo que avivó los temores de que la agencia revisara a la baja sus previsiones de rendimiento.
items.body:
Los futuros del maíz estadounidense se dispararon el martes después de que el Departamento de Agricultura anunciara un recorte mayor de lo esperado en su valoración del estado de la cosecha, lo que avivó los temores de que la agencia revisara a la baja sus previsiones de rendimiento.
Los futuros de la soja también subieron, ya que las recientes lluvias ralentizaron la cosecha y han suscitado inquietudes sobre la calidad de la cosecha y el contenido en aceite.
Por su parte, el trigo subió por cuarta sesión consecutiva, ya que los ataques a buques graneleros en el Mar Negro reforzaron los temores sobre las interrupciones en las exportaciones debido a la guerra de Rusia con Ucrania.
Los operadores de cereales siguen de cerca las previsiones meteorológicas del Medio Oeste, mientras los agricultores intensifican la cosecha tras los retrasos provocados por las lluvias de la semana pasada. Se espera que gran parte de la región se mantenga seca durante la próxima semana.
El Departamento de Agricultura de EEUU (USDA) informó el lunes que, a fecha de domingo, los agricultores estadounidenses habían cosechado el 23% de su maíz y el 25 %de su soja, por debajo de las previsiones de los analistas y del ritmo medio de los últimos cinco años.
La agencia también rebajó más de lo esperado su estimación de las cosechas de maíz calificadas en condiciones de "buenas a excelentes".
"Parece que la calidad de las cosechas se está convirtiendo en un problema cada vez mayor. Y no estoy seguro de que todo el mundo esté convencido, sobre todo en lo que respecta al maíz, de que los rendimientos sean tan buenos como afirma el USDA", señaló Jim Gerlach, presidente de la correduría de materias primas A/C Trading.
El USDA tiene previsto actualizar sus previsiones sobre las cosechas de maíz y soja de EEUU en un reporte mensual de oferta y demanda que se publicará el viernes.
El contrato de maíz de diciembre de la Bolsa de Chicago (CBOT) subía 9,5 centavos a 5,0675 dólares el bushel a las 1745 GMT, mientras que el contrato de soja de noviembre subía 18,5 centavos a 12,9925 dólares el bushel.
El trigo de diciembre de la CBOT subió 10 centavos a 7,0225 dólares el bushel, en medio de las continuas preocupaciones por las interrupciones en el suministro en la región del Mar Negro.
Dos buques mercantes, incluido uno que transportaba cereales, fueron alcanzados el martes por un ataque con drones en el mar Negro, frente a las costas de Bulgaria. Otro buque fue alcanzado el lunes fuera de las aguas territoriales de Rumania, en un ataque que Ucrania atribuyó a drones rusos.

シュミッド氏はオクラホマ州で開催された地域経済イベントで、債券利回りの上昇が借り入れコストを押し上げ、「特定のセクターで若干軟調さがみられるかもしれないが、われわれは短期金利に注目しており、個人的にはまだやるべきことがあると考えている」と述べた。

items.title: Report: Seahawks decide against signing RB Joe Mixon
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: The Seattle Seahawks decided against signing veteran running back Joe Mixon to their practice squad, ESPN reported on Tuesday.
items.body:
The Seattle Seahawks decided against signing veteran running back Joe Mixon to their practice squad, ESPN reported on Tuesday.
Mixon worked out for the Seahawks on Monday and underwent a physical. There is no word on what issue led to Seattle reversing course on Mixon, who will remain a free agent.
The Seahawks' only healthy running backs are Emanuel Wilson, George Holani and Velus Jones. Seattle (3-1) placed rookie running back Jadarian Price, the 32nd overall pick in April's draft, on injured reserve Saturday with a chest injury.
Zach Charbonnet will work in team drills during practice this week but won't play Sunday against the San Francisco 49ers (4-0), head coach Mike Macdonald said.
Mixon, 30, is a two-time Pro Bowler who last played for the Houston Texans in 2024 following seven seasons with the Cincinnati Bengals.
He racked up 1,016 yards, 11 touchdowns and a Pro Bowl nod in his 14 games for the Texans. But Mixon missed the 2025 campaign due to a foot injury and was released last March.
Mixon has gained 7,428 yards and scored 60 touchdowns on the ground in 111 career games (102 starts) since entering the league in 2017. He has added another 2,448 yards and 14 touchdowns on 319 receptions.
Charbonnet, 25, has yet to make his season debut after tearing his ACL on Jan. 17 in the NFC Divisional Round defeat of the 49ers on Seattle's path to a Super Bowl championship.
--Field Level Media

items.title: Líderes de setor de seguros estão divididos sobre responsabilidade por riscos da IA
items.author: Mia Macgregor
items.creator: Mia Macgregor
items.summary: As seguradoras estão divididas quanto às apólices que deveriam cobrir os riscos relacionados à inteligência artificial, mesmo com hackers utilizando IA para ataques, afirmaram os participantes do painel na Cúpula de Risco Digital da NetDiligence, realizada nesta terça-feira.
items.body:
As seguradoras estão divididas quanto às apólices que deveriam cobrir os riscos relacionados à inteligência artificial, mesmo com hackers utilizando IA para ataques, afirmaram os participantes do painel na Cúpula de Risco Digital da NetDiligence, realizada nesta terça-feira.
Os palestrantes da cúpula, realizada na Filadélfia, nos Estados Unidos, discordaram sobre se a exposição à IA é principalmente uma questão digital, uma questão de responsabilidade civil de diretores e executivos ou um novo risco para o qual o setor ainda não encontrou uma recomendação adequada.
“Há tantas coisas que podem dar errado e que vão além da área eletrônica que, basicamente, cheguei à conclusão de que se trata de uma questão de responsabilidade civil de diretores e executivos”, disse Gail Arkin, vice-presidente sênior e diretora jurídica da Berkley Cyber Risk Solutions.
Arkin afirmou que a cobertura de seguro sobre questões digitais não aborda questões como se uma empresa está infringindo os direitos de terceiros, utilizando dados que não tem o direito de usar ou incorporando preconceitos em seus programas. Os conselhos de administração estão elaborando políticas de IA e contratando equipes para monitorar como ela é utilizada, disse ela, o que torna isso “mais do que uma questão tecnológica, honestamente, e definitivamente mais do que uma questão cibernética”.
Tim Nazzaro, gerente global de produtos digitais da Hartford Steam Boiler, dividiu os riscos da IA em três categorias.
Primeiro, riscos relacionados à segurança e à privacidade, como o vazamento de dados pessoais por uma ferramenta de IA. Ele afirmou que a empresa é responsável por isso e que “isso deve estar claramente contemplado em uma apólice de segurança eletrônica”.
A segunda categoria diz respeito a outras linhas de seguro, por exemplo, uma ferramenta de IA que discrimine na contratação se enquadraria em uma apólice de responsabilidade civil por práticas trabalhistas.
A terceira categoria abrange novos riscos que “não têm um lugar definido”, disse Nazzaro. Ele alertou o setor de segurança digital contra o hábito de optar por “ampliar a cobertura, simplesmente incluir o risco, sem fazer a subscrição”.
“Acho que isso poderia ser incluído em uma apólice cibernética, mas, se for o caso, precisamos garantir que estamos avaliando esses riscos”, disse ele. Ele citou as novas regulamentações sobre IA. Multas por violação de regras que não sejam leis de privacidade podem não se enquadrar em uma apólice cibernética, afirmou.
Danielle Roth, líder de prática e chefe de sinistros cibernéticos para a América do Norte na Axa XL, disse que as seguradoras não devem tratar a IA como “um monólito”. Em vez disso, afirmou ela, devem voltar à análise básica da cobertura: quem é o segurado, qual é o sinistro, se ele aciona algum acordo de seguro e se há exclusões aplicáveis.
“Talvez nem saibamos, em caso de violação, se a IA foi usada ou não. Podemos especular, mas talvez nunca venhamos a descobrir”, disse Roth. Ela defendeu que os segurados trabalhem com seus corretores para avaliar seus próprios riscos.
Arkin, da Berkley, comparou a situação a um “risco cibernético silencioso”, observando que “a exposição à IA estará presente em todas as apólices de seguro existentes. No momento, trata-se apenas de uma IA silenciosa”.
EXPLOSÃO DE ATAQUES Michael Brunetti, vice-presidente de resposta a incidentes da MOXFIVE, disse que sua empresa está mais ocupada desde por volta de 4 de julho do que nunca. O ransomware tradicional e a dupla extorsão ainda são comuns, mas os ataques a serviços de computação em nuvem são onde “as coisas estão mudando”, afirmou ele. Ele citou grupos como o ShinyHunters, que têm como alvo aplicativos de software como serviço (SaaS).
Esses grupos não precisam mais invadir uma rede e criptografar tudo, disse Brunetti. Em vez disso, eles usam IA para vasculhar dados roubados em busca do material mais sensível, escrevem mensagens de extorsão que fazem a ameaça “parecer muito mais assustadora” e criam rapidamente perfis de executivos. Um trabalho que costumava levar dias ou semanas agora leva minutos ou horas, afirmou ele.
Roth disse que a Axa XL também teve um verão bastante agitado e observou que grande parte disso se deveu a ataques a escritórios de advocacia, que, segundo ela, substituíram o setor de saúde como alvo preferido. A maioria dos ataques se baseou em phishing, em vez de novas técnicas de IA, disse ela, e os funcionários continuam sendo o maior ponto forte ou o elo mais fraco de uma empresa.

items.title: US appeals court weighs block on Kennedy's vaccine panel appointments
items.author: Nate Raymond
items.creator: Nate Raymond
items.summary: A lawyer for the Trump administration told a federal appeals court on Tuesday that a judge had improperly hamstrung an influential vaccine advisory panel by blocking Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s handpicked appointees from serving on it.
items.body:
A lawyer for the Trump administration told a federal appeals court on Tuesday that a judge had improperly hamstrung an influential vaccine advisory panel by blocking Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.'s handpicked appointees from serving on it.
US Justice Department attorney Matthew Zorn argued at a hearing before the 1st US Circuit Court of Appeals in Boston that the judge's ruling was preventing the Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices from meeting due to concerns that any new appointments Kennedy made to it could also be blocked.
"We're asking the court to vacate the order on the appointments so that the secretary can reconstitute the committee and get it back to work," Zorn said.
Kennedy, an anti-vaccine activist picked by President Donald Trump last year to head the US Department of Health and Human Services, removed and replaced all 17 independent experts who previously served on the panel, which makes recommendations on vaccine policy to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
That action formed the basis of the lawsuit by the American Academy of Pediatrics and other medical groups, which also sought to block other shifts in vaccine policy under Kennedy.
US District Judge Brian Murphy in a [USN:L1N40410J TEXT:"March 16 order"] concluded that Kennedy, in picking new members, did not comply with the Federal Advisory Committee Act, which requires such advisory panels to be balanced, and instead picked "distinctly unqualified" individuals to serve on the committee that is supposed to be composed of experts on vaccines and immunization.
The Trump administration contends that portion of Murphy's order has deprived ACIP of a quorum needed to issue recommendations on flu shots and other vaccines because any newly appointed members would likely require court approval.
Some members of the three-judge appeals court panel on Tuesday raised concerns about how Murphy had crafted his order, which blocked 13 appointees from serving. Chief US Circuit Judge David Barron said it lacked any explanation for why blocking Kennedy's appointees was legally authorized or justified.
"It's hard to know precisely what harm this relief was designed to address," he said.
But Andrew Pincus, a lawyer for the plaintiffs, urged the court to leave it in place, saying Murphy's decision to block 13 of the panel's members from continuing to serve provided "important protection for America's public health."
Murphy in his order also blocked the CDC's January 5 move to cut the number of routinely recommended childhood vaccinations and set aside votes ACIP had taken under Kennedy's watch, including to downgrade recommendations for hepatitis B vaccines for newborns and COVID-19 shots broadly.
The Trump administration [USN:L1N42Q0L9 TEXT:"opted against"] appealing those portions of that ruling by Murphy, an appointee of Democratic President Joe Biden, and instead focused narrowly on his decision blocking the 13 appointees to the vaccine panel.
Since Murphy ruled, ACIP has not met, canceling two meetings so far. Another, set for October 21-23, would likely also be canceled if the committee is not reconstituted before then.

items.title: Video de un avión fue alterado para incluir gritos y no corresponde al incidente de flydubai
items.author: Reuters Fact Check
items.creator: Reuters Fact Check
items.summary: Un video que muestra una ventana de un avión en el que se ven edificaciones costeras y se escuchan gritos no corresponde al incidente reportado el 30 de septiembre en el vuelo de Dubái a Tel Aviv de la aerolínea flydubai, como dicen publicaciones en redes sociales.
items.body:
Un video que muestra una ventana de un avión en el que se ven edificaciones costeras y se escuchan gritos no corresponde al incidente reportado el 30 de septiembre en el vuelo de Dubái a Tel Aviv de la aerolínea flydubai, como dicen publicaciones en redes sociales.
Estos son los datos clave:
Publicaciones en redes sociales compartieron el video alterado el 30 de septiembre con la descripción: “Terror en el aire: copiloto habría apuñalado al capitán en vuelo rumbo a Tel Aviv”.
Horas antes de que se publicara el video, Reuters informó que el vuelo FZ1073 de flydubai fue desviado a Arabia Saudita tras un incidente a bordo.
Posteriormente, las autoridades israelíes [USN:S8N44D013 TEXT:"dijeron"] que el copiloto había apuñalado al capitán para intentar estrellar el avión, pero que los pasajeros y la tripulación lo impidieron.
El video de redes sociales es de otro vuelo de flydubai, que estaba cruzando la costa emiratí en dirección al Aeropuerto Internacional de Dubái.
Los datos del rastreador de vuelos FlightRadar24 muestran que el vuelo FZ1073 viajó en dirección opuesta a la aeronave que aparece en el video y entró brevemente en el espacio aéreo jordano, a casi 2,000 km de Dubái, antes de desviarse hacia Arabia Saudita.
El audio de la gente gritando fue tomado de otro video no relacionado publicado en TikTok en junio de 2022.
Las características geográficas del video de TikTok coinciden con una zona montañosa cerca de Ushuaia, Argentina.
El usuario de TikTok, un DJ argentino llamado Nico Vallorani, dijo en una publicación que grabó el video en un vuelo a Ushuaia, y la gente gritó porque el avión estaba experimentando turbulencias.
Vallorani no respondió a una solicitud de comentarios.
Un análisis realizado con la herramienta de verificación de Meta Platforms, que detecta marcas de agua invisibles incrustadas en el contenido multimedia generado, determinó que el video probablemente fue editado o creado utilizando los modelos de IA de la empresa tecnológica.
Veredicto: Alterado. El audio y las imágenes se han editado a partir de fuentes separadas, y no corresponden al incidente aéreo ocurrido en el vuelo FZ1073 el 30 de septiembre de 2026.
Reuters Fact Check ofrece información confiable mediante su canal de WhatsApp para  México . Envíenos un mensaje con el contenido en español que desea que verifiquemos.
Este artículo fue realizado por el equipo de Reuters Fact Check. Lea más sobre nuestro trabajo de verificación de afirmaciones en las redes sociales.

items.title: Los hitos que revelará la Semana Mundial del Espacio 2026
items.author: Fátima Romero
items.summary: El tema de este año es la Revolución de los Cohetes, que busca destacar cómo el mayor acceso al espacio y la reducción de los costos de lanzamiento han impulsado el sector espacial y permitido el desa ...
items.body: Bloomberg Línea — La Semana Mundial del Espacio 2026 se celebra del 4 al 10 de octubre bajo el lema “Revolución de los cohetes” (Rocket Revolution), dedicado este año a las tecnologías que están cambiando la forma en que la humanidad llega al espacio, que abarca propulsores reutilizables, nuevos vehículos de lanzamiento y una industria espacial comercial en expansión. Ver más: SpaceX lanza telescopio espacial de la NASA destinado a la búsqueda de energía oscura La Asamblea General de la ONU estableció esta conmemoración en 1999, en la resolución 54/68, del 6 de diciembre de ese año, para celebrar cada año las contribuciones de la ciencia y la tecnología espaciales a la mejora de la condición humana. Las fechas elegidas responden a dos hitos: el 4 de octubre de 1957 la Unión Soviética puso en órbita el Sputnik 1, el primer satélite artificial de la Tierra, y el 10 de octubre de 1967 entró en vigor el Tratado del Espacio Ultraterrestre, que sentó los principios de la exploración del espacio con fines pacíficos. El tema de este año “reconoce cómo el mayor acceso al espacio y la caída de los precios de lanzamiento han estimulado el ecosistema espacial y sus nuevas aplicaciones”, explicó en un comunicado Dennis Stone, presidente de la Asociación de la Semana Mundial del Espacio, quien añadió que la elección busca también despertar vocaciones científicas y técnicas entre los estudiantes. Durante décadas, alcanzar la órbita exigió enormes cantidades de combustible e infraestructura y cohetes diseñados para un solo vuelo. Ver más: SpaceX propone construir un gasoducto para abastecer de combustible a sus cohetes Starship Ese modelo está cambiando, con los propulsores reutilizables han demostrado que partes de un lanzador pueden regresar a la Tierra y volver a volar, mientras un número creciente de empresas y países desarrolla nuevas vías de acceso orbital. El ejemplo más reciente lo protagonizó el Starship de SpaceX ( SPCX ), que alcanzó la órbita por primera vez en su vuelo de prueba del 28 de septiembre desde Starbase, en Texas, EE.UU., y desplegó 26 satélites Starlink V3. La misión se acortó por un problema en un motor, pero cumplió sus dos objetivos principales: llegar a órbita y liberar su carga. El cambio no se limita a construir cohetes más potentes. La reutilización y las nuevas arquitecturas de lanzamiento pueden modificar la economía y la cadencia de los vuelos espaciales, mientras los lanzadores de menor tamaño amplían las opciones de organizaciones con presupuestos más ajustados. El resultado es un sector con más participantes y una gama más amplia de misiones, desde comunicaciones y observación de la Tierra hasta naves científicas y vuelo tripulado. Los sistemas espaciales ya sustentan servicios cotidianos como la navegación, la meteorología, la vigilancia ambiental y la respuesta ante desastres, uno de los mensajes que la semana quiere subrayar. Los organizadores esperan actividades en más de un centenar de países, incluyendo charlas, exposiciones, sesiones de cine, eventos astronómicos y proyectos prácticos de ciencia y tecnología. Entre los programas destacados figura la colaboración entre la Agencia Espacial Europea (ESA) y The Pokémon Company International, con exposiciones en centros de la agencia y museos de toda Europa y actividades dentro del juego Pokémon GO. La astronauta francesa Sophie Adenot llevó incluso un peluche de Pikachu a la Estación Espacial Internacional como parte de la campaña. El complejo de visitantes del Kennedy Space Center, en Florida, acogerá el 9 de octubre una exposición con la NASA y socios industriales, mientras estudiantes y clubes de modelismo lanzarán cohetes a pequeña escala con equipos cedidos por United Launch Alliance y Estes. La plataforma BBC StoryWorks conmemorará el evento con el estreno online de su próxima serie ‘Space Renaissance’. Para llevar el tema a las aulas, Estes Education y la organización de la Semana crearon el “Rocket Revolution Toolkit”, un paquete de actividades para escuelas que incluye el reto de diseñar vehículos de lanzamiento reutilizables. En España, el Planetario de Madrid, el Hemisfèric de València y el Parque de las Ciencias de Granada, entre otros centros, han programado proyecciones, charlas, talleres y observaciones astronómicas gratuitas, en su mayoría de entrada libre hasta completar aforo. La ESA acoge además exposiciones de la colaboración con Pokémon en su centro ESAC de Villanueva de la Cañada.

items.title: EPA air chief leaves agency after overseeing Trump regulatory rollback
items.author: Jarrett Renshaw, Siddharth Cavale
items.creator: Jarrett Renshaw, Siddharth Cavale
items.summary: The Environmental Protection Agency official who has overseen some of the Trump administration's most consequential efforts to roll back climate and air pollution regulations resigned effective last week, the agency said on Tuesday.
items.body:
The Environmental Protection Agency official who has overseen some of the Trump administration's most consequential efforts to roll back climate and air pollution regulations resigned effective last week, the agency said on Tuesday.
Aaron Szabo, an attorney who led the EPA's Office of Air and Radiation since 2025 as an assistant administrator, departed on Friday. The EPA had previously said Szabo would leave in July but asked him to remain longer. Reuters reported at the time that his planned [USN:L6N43U131 TEXT:"move to a law firm"] had fallen through.
At EPA, Szabo oversaw programs covering air pollution, vehicle emissions, blending gasoline with renewable fuels and other major Clean Air Act provisions.
During his tenure, the EPA moved to repeal its 2009 finding that greenhouse gases endanger public health and welfare, a step that could substantially limit its authority to regulate climate pollution. The office also worked on rolling back emissions rules covering power plants, vehicles and the oil and gas industry.
The EPA, in an email to Reuters, thanked Szabo for his “tremendous work” advancing President Donald Trump's agenda. The agency said his office helped deliver “the single largest deregulatory action in U.S. history” and valued deregulatory cost savings during Szabo's tenure at more than $1.6 trillion.
The EPA said Justin Schwab, who serves as a senior adviser to EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin, has been nominated to replace Szabo.
Szabo and Schwab did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

items.title: Mike Flanagan reimagina “Carrie” para uma nova geração que enfrenta cyberbullying e simulações de tiroteio nas escolas
items.author: Meriam Telhig
items.creator: Meriam Telhig
items.summary: “Carrie” retorna nesta semana em uma nova adaptação de oito episódios do cineasta de terror Mike Flanagan, que reinterpreta a história clássica do autor Stephen King para o público moderno por meio das redes sociais, do cyberbullying e dos simulados de ataque com atirador ativo.
items.body:
“Carrie” retorna nesta semana em uma nova adaptação de oito episódios do cineasta de terror Mike Flanagan, que reinterpreta a história clássica do autor Stephen King para o público moderno por meio das redes sociais, do cyberbullying e dos simulados de ataque com atirador ativo.
Em entrevista à Reuters, Flanagan disse que nunca imaginou revisitar “Carrie”, mas sua perspectiva mudou quando seu filho estava se preparando para entrar no ensino médio.
“Havia tantas ideias em ‘Carrie’ que parecem ainda mais relevantes hoje do que há meio século, quando o livro foi escrito”, disse Flanagan. “Achei que poderíamos fazer algo realmente novo com isso.”
A série acompanha uma adolescente socialmente isolada que luta para se integrar no ensino médio enquanto lida com um relacionamento complicado com sua mãe superprotetora, interpretada por Samantha Sloyan. A adaptação atualiza o romance de King, de 1974, com questões enfrentadas pelos adolescentes de agora.
Summer H. Howell, que interpreta Carrie White, disse que, a princípio, ficou intimidada ao assumir um papel tão icônico, mas que a oportunidade de explorar a personagem ao longo de oito episódios a atraiu.
“Foi um pouco intimidador”, disse Howell. “Mas então percebi que eles estavam buscando algo diferente com essa Carrie, e que havia mais tempo para explorar a história dela.”
Matthew Lillard, que interpreta o diretor Henry Grayle, disse que os temas da série ressoaram nele como pai, devido ao assédio online e às pressões que os adolescentes enfrentam.
“Meus filhos estão sujeitos aos horríveis trolls que vivem nas trevas da internet”, disse Lillard.
Alison Thornton, que interpreta a antagonista de Carrie, Chris Hargensen, disse que as redes sociais mudaram a natureza do bullying.
“As pessoas se sentem muito mais à vontade para praticar bullying online do que pessoalmente”, disse Thornton. “Elas não precisam realmente enfrentar as consequências.”
Flanagan disse que queria que cada personagem de “Carrie” parecesse real e complexo, ao mesmo tempo em que explorava as escolhas que as pessoas fazem entre crueldade e bondade.
Sloyan disse que a série também destaca a responsabilidade pessoal.
“Também acho que ele está colocando em destaque o fato de que temos escolha e que existe uma autonomia que podemos exercer nesse contexto”, disse ela, acrescentando que a série explora “a humanidade envolvida”.
Howell disse que a série, no fim das contas, transmite uma mensagem simples: “Sejam gentis uns com os outros, mesmo quando vocês mesmos não estiverem se sentindo bem”.
“Carrie” estará disponível globalmente no Amazon Prime Video a partir de quarta-feira.

items.title: US EIA lifts Brent forecast to $98 as Iran war tightens global supplies
items.author: ETMarkets.com
items.summary: The US Energy Information Administration has revised its oil price forecasts for the coming years due to supply issues. Global benchmark Brent crude is expected to average approximately $98 a barrel in 2026. Retail diesel prices are projected to remain high initially before gradually declining to around $4.50 in 2027. Improvements in Middle Eastern oil production are anticipated as transit routes become safer and more efficient.
items.body: The US Energy Information Administration raised its oil price forecasts for this year and next on Tuesday, citing rapidly declining global inventories and tight diesel supplies caused by the ongoing war with Iran, Reuters reported.The EIA now expects global benchmark Brent crude to average about $98 a barrel in 2026, an 8% increase from its previous projection, according to its latest Short-Term Energy Outlook.Oil and fuel prices have surged since the US-Israeli war with Iran disrupted shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, which handled about 20% of global oil supplies before the conflict. Iran has also targeted regional energy infrastructure in retaliation for US military strikes.Falling inventories and tight diesel supplies are expected to keep prices elevated. Brent is forecast to average about $105 a barrel in the fourth quarter, $14 above the EIA’s earlier estimate.US retail diesel prices, which reached record highs last month, are projected to remain above $6 a gallon in October before gradually declining to an average of about $4.50 in 2027.However, Middle Eastern oil production and exports are expected to recover gradually as transit through the Strait of Hormuz improves and producers increasingly use alternative export routes and ship-to-ship transfers.As supply flows normalise and inventories rebuild, Brent is expected to average $84 a barrel in 2027, $10 above the agency’s previous forecast.According to Reuters, regional oil flows have improved after Saudi Arabia resumed shipments through its East-West Pipeline to the Red Sea, bypassing the Strait of Hormuz. Exporters have also adapted to attacks on shipping and energy infrastructure through “dark transits,” in which tankers switch off their tracking systems before transferring cargo at sea.These measures helped restore Gulf oil flows, excluding Iran, to more than 81% of pre-war levels in September.As the workarounds expand, crude-production shutdowns are expected to decline from 4.5 million barrels per day in the fourth quarter of 2026 to 2.7 million barrels per day in the first quarter of 2027, the EIA said.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

items.author: CNA
items.summary: CERNOBBIO, Italy, Oct 6 : Euroleague shareholder clubs rejected a collaboration offer from the NBA on Tuesday, according to sources familiar with the discussions, raising the prospect of a battle for the continent's biggest teams, players and commercial riches.The door on a deal has yet to be closed though.

CERNOBBIO, Italy, Oct 6 : Euroleague shareholder clubs rejected a collaboration offer from the NBA on Tuesday, according to sources familiar with the discussions, raising the prospect of a battle for the continent's biggest teams, players and commercial riches.
The door on a deal has yet to be closed though.
The Euroleague said in a statement that its 13 shareholder clubs had agreed to convert into franchises, a change that would turn their current licences into a more lasting stake in the league. The clubs did not, however, take a formal decision on expanding the competition from 20 to 24 teams.
Regarding Euroleague's expansion plan, a person attending the meeting told Reuters the decision on allocating additional long-term licences would be taken within the next month.

The source said the Euroleague was keen to move ahead with expansion and attention will now be on whether the NBA submits a fresh proposal before those calls are made.
Up to eight additional long-term licences could be awarded. The remaining places would be filled through a combination of short-term licences, wildcards and sporting qualification through the BKT EuroCup.
A senior sports executive told Reuters any collaboration between Euroleague and the NBA was unlikely before 2028 because of the difficulty of organising a new competition in time for the 2027-28 season.
Representatives of the 13 permanent shareholder clubs met near Lake Como to discuss the expansion plan, with the prospect of an agreement with the NBA dominating discussions around the future of European basketball.
The Euroleague did not mention the widely reported NBA offer in its statement, but told Reuters last Friday it remained open to collaboration. Although the clubs rejected the current proposal, talks with the NBA could continue.
Reuters was not immediately able to confirm the details of the NBA's offer but media reports said it would have seen the NBA's continental expansion project merge with Euroleague.
The NBA did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment. NBA Europe's managing director, George Aivazoglou, is due to speak at a conference in London on Thursday.
The rejection is a significant setback to attempts to unite Europe’s established elite basketball competition with the financial and commercial power of the NBA, which plans to launch a 16-team NBA Europe league in 2027.
SURGE OF INTEREST
The NBA has stepped up its push into Europe amid a surge of interest in the sport, with Euroleague reporting in May an 82 per cent increase in TV viewership through the first 25 regular-season rounds of the 2025-26 campaign.
The NBA has also enjoyed growing momentum on the continent. Streaming deals with providers like Amazon Prime have boosted audiences for the NBA in Europe, while regular-season games in Berlin and London this year highlighted the league's growing appeal.
Viewership of January's clash between Orlando Magic and Memphis Grizzlies in London was up 90 per cent compared to the last NBA game there in 2019.
A report from JB Capital commissioned by the Euroleague values the competition at €1.41 billion ($1.59 billion), while the aggregate value of its licensed teams was put at approximately €1.8 billion.
Those figures pale in comparison to the NBA.
The NBA recently surpassed Major League Baseball to become the world's second-richest sports league, according to Sports Value, a marketing and valuation agency, with upwards of $14 billion in revenue during the 2025-26 season.
The NBA and Euroleague have said throughout this year that they would like to work together on a new competition, but each has also made clear it is prepared to pursue its own plans if no agreement is reached.
No deadline has been set for a deal, although the sides have indicated they want greater clarity by the end of the season.
($1 = 0.8883 euros)
(Additional reporting by Amy Tennery and Ruairidh Barlow, editing by Ed Osmond, Ken Ferris and Toby Davis)

items.title: Governo reduz a US$84,4 bi projeção de superávit comercial em 2026 apesar de dado forte em setembro
items.author: Bernardo Caram
items.creator: Bernardo Caram
items.summary: O Ministério do Desenvolvimento, Indústria, Comércio e Serviços (MDIC) reduziu nesta terça-feira sua projeção para o superávit da balança comercial brasileira em 2026 a US$84,4 bilhões, contra previsão feita em julho de saldo de US$90,0 bilhões, prevendo ganho menor nas exportações com o arrefecimento de preços internacionais.
items.body:
O Ministério do Desenvolvimento, Indústria, Comércio e Serviços (MDIC) reduziu nesta terça-feira sua projeção para o superávit da balança comercial brasileira em 2026 a US$84,4 bilhões, contra previsão feita em julho de saldo de US$90,0 bilhões, prevendo ganho menor nas exportações com o arrefecimento de preços internacionais.
Apesar da revisão para baixo, o resultado ainda seria 24% mais forte do que o observado no ano anterior, quando o saldo foi de US$68,1 bilhões, e marcaria o segundo maior saldo da série histórica, atrás apenas do dado de 2023.
Pelos cálculos do MDIC, as exportações devem fechar o ano em US$382,5 bilhões, uma redução de US$11,9 bilhões em relação à estimativa de julho, mas ainda representando um recorde histórico. As importações ficariam em US$298,1 bilhões, um recuo de US$6,3 bilhões sobre a previsão anterior.
O diretor de Estatísticas e Estudos de Comércio Exterior do MDIC, Herlon Brandão, afirmou que a projeção feita em julho refletia forte alta dos preços do petróleo e de outros produtos diante da guerra no Irã, o que ampliaria o resultado das exportações. A partir do meio do ano, segundo ele, parte desses preços registrou alguma acomodação, o que reflete na nova projeção.
“Esse movimento arrefeceu e resultou em uma taxa de crescimento (das exportações) ainda significativa, mas um pouco menor do que o modelo estava captando no primeiro semestre”, disse.
DADOS DE SETEMBRO O MDIC apontou que a balança comercial brasileira registrou em setembro um superávit de US$7,741 bilhões, um crescimento de 146% na comparação com o resultado do mesmo mês de 2025 e melhor do que o esperado pelo mercado, que previa em pesquisa da Reuters um saldo positivo de US$7,191 bilhões. (BRTBAL=ECI)
O desempenho do mês é fruto de US$34,418 bilhões em exportações, uma alta de 12,9% na comparação com o mesmo mês de 2025, e US$26,678 bilhões em importações, recuo de 2,4%.
No período, houve aumento das exportações em todos os setores, com destaque para uma alta de 39,8% na indústria extrativa, seguida de crescimentos de 5,3% na indústria de transformação e de 4,8% na agropecuária.
Entre os destaques estão os embarques de óleos brutos de petróleo, com crescimento de 77% no período, de soja, com alta de 12%, e óleos combustíveis de petróleo, com alta de 39%. No sentido contrário, houve redução de quase 31% nas vendas de carne bovina.
Em setembro, as exportações aos Estados Unidos cresceram 32%, apesar da vigência do tarifaço, que atinge 23% da pauta de produtos vendidos, segundo Brandão. Ele ressaltou altas de 524% nas vendas de carne e de 108% nos embarques de café para o país norte-americano, produtos que eram taxados em setembro do ano passado e estão agora isentos de tarifas.
Para a China, houve recuo de 7,6% nas exportações no mês, diante de tarifação das vendas de carne bovina após o atingimento de cota, mas também por uma redução na demanda do país, segundo Brandão, que impactou as vendas de minério de ferro, soja e milho.
Do lado das importações, houve queda mais intensa nas compras bens de capital, um recuo de 30% motivado pela importação de plataforma de petróleo em setembro de 2025, que distorceu a base de comparação com o mês passado.
Houve ainda queda de 2,4% nas importações de bens intermediários, enquanto foram registradas altas de 11,5% em bens de consumo e de 41,2% em combustíveis.
Nos primeiros nove meses do ano, o país acumulou um superávit comercial de US$62,396 bilhões, 35% acima do saldo positivo de US$46,300 bilhões do mesmo período de 2025.

items.title: Fed plans bank-supervision overhaul to strengthen accountability, says Vice Chair Michelle Bowman
items.author: ETMarkets.com
items.summary: The Federal Reserve is set to realign its bank supervision system for increased accountability and efficient decision-making. Five new geographic supervisory regions will be established, each led by a regional leader. This new structure aims to address concerns raised in an independent review of Silicon Valley Bank’s collapse. The Fed will also reconsider asset thresholds for regulatory requirements to better align with inflation and economic growth.
items.body: The Federal Reserve plans to restructure its supervision of US banks, replacing a system that gives regional Fed presidents responsibility for examinations with one that gives Washington officials clearer accountability, its top regulatory official said on Tuesday, Reuters reported.Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman said the central bank will establish five geographic supervisory regions, each headed by a new “regional leader.”Officials in Washington currently set the examination policy, while the Fed’s 12 regional banks conduct and oversee the supervision of financial institutions.In prepared remarks for a conference at the St. Louis Fed, Bowman said the existing structure “disincentivised a critical link between responsibility and accountability.” She cited an independent review of Silicon Valley Bank’s collapse that she commissioned and that found Fed examiners were slow to act.“The Federal Reserve supervisory function will be realigned to implement a culture of accountability and clear decision-making authority,” Bowman said.Under the new structure, regional leaders will be responsible for all supervisory activity within their territories, although staff at the regional Reserve Banks will continue conducting examinations. Regional Fed presidents currently oversee supervision within their respective districts.Bowman also criticised the Fed’s reliance on committees to supervise banks, arguing that the system delayed action and blurred responsibility when problems emerged. She said the use of such committees should be streamlined.“In practice, these committees became a source for plausible deniability and a disincentive for examiners to take prompt and decisive action to address identified risks,” she said.Asset thresholds under reviewBowman has launched a broad overhaul of how the Fed regulates the country’s largest and most complex banks. Since becoming the central bank’s top regulatory official in 2025, she has replaced supervisory leaders, reduced staff and issued guidelines narrowing the issues examiners should investigate.She has argued that bank examiners should concentrate on material financial risks rather than minor procedural deficiencies.Bowman also said the Fed will consider revising the asset thresholds that determine when banks become subject to stricter requirements.The proposed changes could allow banks more room to expand before triggering additional capital, liquidity and stress-testing rules.The Fed will examine its fixed-dollar asset thresholds and consider a mechanism to update them every five years to account for inflation and economic growth, Bowman said.Banks have long argued that fixed thresholds become outdated and can impose stricter regulations on institutions that were not originally intended to face such oversight.(Disclaimer: This article is based on inputs from agencies. These do not represent the views of The Economic Times)

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [６日　ロイター] -
items.body:
[６日　ロイター] - 米サンフランシスコ地区連銀のデイリー総裁は６日、今後の追加利上げの是非について、インフレを押し上げてきたショックが収束に向かうのか、逆にショックが相互に重なり合って持続するのかに大きく左右されるとの考えを示した。 

デイリー総裁はアクシオスとのインタビューで、９月の連邦公開市場委員会（ＦＯＭＣ）ではインフレリスクの高まりを受けて利上げを支持したと説明。その上で「われわれが経験してきたショック、つまり関税措置、中東紛争に伴う原油価格の急騰、そしてＡＩ（人工知能）が一時的な影響しか及ぼさない従来型のショックであると判明すれば、追加利上げは不要かもしれない。私は依然としてその可能性を一定程度想定している」と語った。

さらに「ただ、これらのショックが互いに相乗効果を生むか、あるいはわれわれの予想より長引くのであれば、もし第２弾の関税交渉が行われてさらなる関税が課されれば、最初のショックに第２のショックが重なることになる。そうなればこれらのショックが影響を及ぼす期間が長引くことになるだろう」と述べた。

デイリー氏は、ＡＩ関連の半導体需要が高まっており、これがインフレ圧力を押し上げ、ショックの影響をより長期化させる可能性があるとの見方も示した。

同総裁は今年のＦＯＭＣで投票権は持っていない。

items.title: Yemeni government fighters shown driving vehicles over Houthi opponents
items.author: Edward Carron
items.creator: Edward Carron
items.summary: Video posted by government forces in Yemen showed them driving armoured cars over Houthi fighters as they recaptured areas around the vital Bab el-Mandeb Strait from the Iran-backed group on Monday in a deadly new phase of the fragmented country's war.
items.body:
Video posted by government forces in Yemen showed them driving armoured cars over Houthi fighters as they recaptured areas around the vital [USN:L8N4520BL TEXT:"Bab el-Mandeb Strait"] from the Iran-backed group on Monday in a deadly new phase of the fragmented country's war.
The videos gave a glimpse into the brutal closing stages of a pitched battle for control of territory near the strait that the Houthis had captured last month. The Houthi advance sent shockwaves through the oil market and pushed up petrol and diesel prices worldwide.
Fighting continued near Bab el-Mandeb on Tuesday as Saudi-backed government forces battled to consolidate [USN:L1N45R06H TEXT:"Monday's counter-attack"], besieging Houthi fighters at a military camp near the strait and pushing into hills to the east, Yemeni military sources said.
The videos, verified by Reuters and filmed from inside the armoured vehicles, showed them striking fighters with their vehicles. Some were armed and some were walking or running. However, others were unarmed and some were sitting, lying or crouching on the sandy shore and made no move to evade the oncoming vehicle as they were run over.
At one point, a vehicle hits a man, running and unarmed, and another crouching on the ground. It then loops back to drive over two men, both with their hands up and unarmed. Shooting can be heard during the video and at one point the vehicle's windscreen is cracked by a gunshot.
A Houthi statement decried the videos as proof of war crimes, saying they showed "the true nature of the Saudi regime and the forces it has mobilised from extremist factions".
Asil al-Saqladi, spokesperson for the Giants Brigade — the main Yemeni government force involved in the fighting at Bab el-Mandeb this week — said the force was conducting an investigation into the incident.
He added that the brigade had been misled into believing that the Houthi fighters there were surrendering but that some of them had then fired on the government force.
The Saudi-led coalition backing the government forces in Yemen did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the videos or the Houthi accusations of war crimes.
The Homeland Shield Forces, a significant formation in the Yemeni government's military coalition, did not comment directly on the videos but issued a directive on Tuesday urging troops to treat prisoners well and adhere to religious, ethical and legal standards.
Rights groups have previously accused the Houthis of war crimes, including sniper and shelling attacks on civilian targets, seizures of aid, abuse of prisoners and use of child soldiers. The group has denied war crimes.
'TURNING POINT' Reuters has not been able to independently verify the extent of government gains and the Houthis denied they had lost ground, saying the government claims of advances were baseless.
Intense fighting meanwhile continued around Yemen's third-largest city of Taiz, where Houthi gains in a mountain district have in recent days cut off a main road to Aden, leaving government forces encircled.
Yemen's [USN:L6N3Y307N TEXT:"civil war"] pits the Houthis against an uneasy coalition of sometimes rival military forces under the internationally recognised government, backed by Saudi Arabia and its allies.
The renewed clashes have added a new front to the Iran-US conflict , with the [USN:L6N45308G TEXT:"US rebuffing"] Saudi requests for military help to reverse Houthi gains on the Red Sea coast near Bab el-Mandeb last month and end the group's missile and drone attacks on their territory.
"The operation itself is significant because it's a turning point in the trajectory of the conflict between the Houthis and the Saudi-led coalition," said Ahmed Nagi, Yemen analyst at International Crisis Group.
"The biggest test will be when they move towards the mountains," he added.
RELIGIOUS AND REGIONAL FAULTLINES The Giants Brigade is a southern military formation originally formed by students at ultra-conservative Sunni Muslim religious colleges.
That background gives both a religious and regional edge to their enmity with the Houthis, who originate in north Yemen and belong to the Zaydi school of Shi'ite Islam.
The Giants have themselves fractured this year, splitting between factions backed by Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates, illustrating the internal divisions that have long beset the Yemeni government's efforts to fight the Houthis.
As well as further squeezing global trade routes after Iran's disruption of shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, the conflagration in Yemen has brought the conflict more directly to Saudi Arabia, a US ally.
The Houthis have repeatedly targeted Saudi infrastructure, including airports, oil refineries and pipelines. Residents of the Saudi capital Riyadh reported hearing booms overnight and two of the kingdom's [USN:L1N45S0BG TEXT:"southern airports"] were targeted.
Saudi Arabia's intervention in the latest wave of fighting included intense air strikes on Houthi forces on Monday as the Giants Brigade advanced along the flat coastal strip towards Bab el-Mandeb.

items.title: MetLife y CNP muestran interés en negocios de Prudential en Brasil y México por US$3.000 millones
items.author: Cristiane Lucchesi, Matheus Piovesana, Alex Rajbhandari
items.summary: Prudential busca obtener US$3.000 millones por las operaciones de Brasil y México en conjunto, con Brasil representando casi el 90% del paquete, según fuentes.
items.body: Bloomberg — Los negocios de Prudential Financial Inc. en Brasil y México han atraído el interés de MetLife Inc. y CNP Assurances SA en una operación que podría reportar unos US$3.000 millones a Prudential, según fuentes familiarizadas con el asunto. Mapfre SA también mostró interés anteriormente, pero no está claro si presentará una oferta, indicaron las fuentes, que pidieron no ser identificadas porque se trata de información privada. Daiichi Life Group Inc. decidió por ahora no presentar una oferta, agregaron. Ver más: Banco Mundial se alinea con pronósticos para el crecimiento de México en 2026 Se espera que la transacción se anuncie este año, aunque las condiciones y los posibles compradores aún podrían cambiar, según las fuentes. Prudential busca obtener US$3.000 millones por las operaciones de Brasil y México en conjunto, con Brasil representando casi el 90% del paquete, según las fuentes. Representantes de Prudential, MetLife, CNP, Daiichi y Mapfre declinaron hacer comentarios. Prudential vende seguros de vida en Brasil y se encuentra entre las mayores aseguradoras del país, con 4.880 millones de reales (US$977 millones) en primas entre enero y julio, según datos del regulador Susep. Cualquier comprador probablemente tendrá que lidiar con demandas laborales pendientes contra Prudential en Brasil, según una de las fuentes. La empresa busca revertir las provisiones vinculadas a esas demandas para pagar un dividendo a su matriz antes del cierre de la operación. Algunos posibles compradores, sin embargo, quieren descontar esas provisiones del precio. Prudential tenía casi 193 millones de reales provisionados por demandas laborales en junio de 2026, según sus estados financieros. Prudential, con sede en Newark, Nueva Jersey, busca simplificar sus operaciones mediante la venta de activos en mercados emergentes. El director ejecutivo, Andy Sullivan, pretende reducir la presencia de la compañía y reasignar recursos hacia negocios menos intensivos en capital para impulsar las ganancias. La directora financiera, Yanela Frias, dijo el mes pasado que la venta de las unidades de Brasil y México estaba “muy avanzada”. Lee más en Bloomberg.com

Oct 6 : U.S. Ryder Cup captain Jim Furyk conceded on Tuesday that his team's dismal foursomes record was "not an anomaly" and promised changes ahead of next year's competition at Adare Manor where they will try to deny Europe a third consecutive victory.
The U.S. have won only three of 16 foursomes matches across the last two editions of the biennial Ryder Cup and also struggled in the same format at the last two Presidents Cups where they went 5-13-0 against a lineup of international players from outside Europe.
"There's some issues. We understand that. Not something I'm very happy with," Furyk, speaking alongside Team Europe captain Luke Donald, said during a press conference at Adare Manor in Limerick, Ireland. "I plan on making some changes."
Furyk, who was named captain of the US team in April after Tiger Woods declined the role following his arrest on a driving-under-the-influence charge, has already implemented a revamped qualification system for the 2027 matches and counts a new analytics team among the changes he hopes will lead to success in foursomes.

Still, his squad will face a tall order at Adare Manor given the US have not won a Ryder Cup on European soil since 1993 at The Belfry in Warwickshire.
"I will promise you, we will be prepared. I'm going to ask this team to do more than any other United States team has in the past," said Furyk. "We'll be prepared. We'll be ready to go in that format, and hopefully we can showcase our talent. We have too much depth to have that poor record in alternate shot."
US Presidents Cup captain Brandt Snedeker fired an early battle cry after his players delivered the most lopsided singles session in that event's history, boasting after the 17-13 triumph that the American team is "going to be a problem" for Europe at the next Ryder Cup.
Donald, who next year will aim to become the first captain to guide a team to three straight Ryder Cup victories, was not about to disagree.
"I have zero complacency about how strong the US are going to be. They always are. On paper, they tend to be stronger than us through the world rankings," said Donald.
"Obviously we have a great record at home but again, zero complacency. You know, I've seen what Jim has been doing behind the scenes, changing the stats, changing the qualification system. He is very, very motivated to come here and put up a good fight."

Source: Reuters

items.title: All-Star pitcher 'Sudden Sam' McDowell dies at 84
items.author: Reuters
items.creator: Reuters
items.summary: Six-time All-Star pitcher Sam McDowell, who played 15 seasons in the majors with four teams, died Monday at the age of 84.
items.body:
Six-time All-Star pitcher Sam McDowell, who played 15 seasons in the majors with four teams, died Monday at the age of 84.
McDowell, a left-hander nicknamed "Sudden Sam" for his brilliant fastball, spent his first 11 seasons in Cleveland from 1961-71. He led the American League in strikeouts five times during that span, including two seasons with more than 300, and topped the league in ERA once.
"The Cleveland Guardians family is deeply saddened by the loss of one of the great pitchers in baseball history, Sam McDowell," Bob DiBiasio, the Guardians' senior vice president of public affairs, said in a press release Tuesday.
"He was a cherished member of our Alumni Ambassador program and loved sharing stories with our fans when he visited Progressive Field," DiBiasio continued. "Most importantly, Sam's life was a story of redemption. After extensive education and training, Sam was a counselor for athletes suffering from addiction and depression. We send our condolences to the entire McDowell family, as well as his many teammates and other organizations impacted by his career."
A Pittsburgh native, McDowell compiled a record of 141-134 with 14 saves and a 3.17 ERA in 425 career games (346 starts) with Cleveland, the San Francisco Giants (1972-73), New York Yankees (1973-74) and his hometown Pirates (1975).
McDowell finished third in the AL Cy Young Award voting in 1970 after finishing 20-12 with a 2.92 ERA and 304 strikeouts in 305 innings.
He racked up 2,159 of his 2,453 strikeouts with Cleveland, joining Hall of Famer Bob Feller (2,581) as the only pitchers in team history with more than 2,000.
--Field Level Media

items.body:
Nvidia-backed cloud-computing company Lambda is raising up to $4 billion at a pre-money valuation of $14.5 billion in what would be its final funding round before a planned initial public offering, the Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday, citing people familiar with the matter.
Here are more details:
Investment firms Blackstone (BX.N) and Coatue Management are leading the round, the report said.
Lambda is aiming to go public in 2027, depending on execution and market conditions, according to a letter to the company's limited partners reviewed by the Journal.
The company's backlog of unfilled orders grew to $50 billion in September from $15 billion in June, according to the letter.
Lambda did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

items.title: US agency to rewrite rules to address vehicle headlight glare
items.author: David Shepardson
items.creator: David Shepardson
items.summary: The US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said on Tuesday that it will rewrite its vehicle lighting standards to address concerns about headlight glare and allow for the latest safety-improving lighting technologies.
items.body:
The US National Highway Traffic Safety Administration said on Tuesday that it will rewrite its vehicle lighting standards to address concerns about headlight glare and allow for the latest safety-improving lighting technologies.
NHTSA said it plans to improve rules for LEDs, dusk sensors, automatic high beams and replaceable light sources. The agency will also evaluate headlamp height and aim and how they impact driver visibility and address headlight glare and make appropriate changes.
Complaints about glare from headlights have increased and some lawmakers have urged the government to set a maximum headlight brightness standard. A growing number of taller trucks and SUVs on roads has also led to more complaints about glare.
LEDs, which now account for most headlights in new cars, are much brighter than traditional halogen headlights.
“Today’s standards do not allow automakers to deploy the latest safety-improving lighting technologies, so we are bringing key experts and stakeholders together to modernize our standards and address potential causes of glare," said NHTSA Administrator Jonathan Morrison.
The issue still accounts for a small number of nighttime crashes, according to a study last year from the Insurance Institute for Highway Safety.
The study noted that headlight glare contributes to far fewer crashes than insufficient visibility. From 2015 to 2023, headlight glare was cited as a factor in only one or two out of every 1,000 nighttime crashes across 11 US states, the study shows.
Federal headlight standards for minimum and maximum brightness have not changed since 1997, IIHS noted. The study found that drivers older than 70 appear to be most affected by headlight glare.
In 2022, NHTSA said it would allow automakers to install adaptive driving beam headlights on new vehicles. The devices adjust the headlight beam pattern to dim portions directed at other vehicles.
NHTSA will use a negotiated rulemaking process to update its vehicle lighting standards. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy will appoint up to 18 people from vehicle lighting manufacturers, motor vehicle equipment associations, safety organizations, research institutions, and engineering associations to take part.

Oct 6 : Captain Shreyas Iyer hit a century as India beat the West Indies by eight wickets in the first Twenty20 of their five-match series in Lucknow on Tuesday.
Iyer led the chase with an unbeaten 102 off 43 deliveries, hitting 10 fours and six sixes, as India cruised to victory with 32 balls to spare.
Abhishek Sharma provided an early burst before Roston Chase dismissed him for 21 off 10 balls. Sanju Samson departed soon after, leaving India at 35 for two.
Iyer and Ishan Kishan then wrested control of the chase, combining in an unbroken 137-run partnership off 67 deliveries to seal victory for India.

NEW YORK, Oct 6 : Oil prices were little changed on Tuesday after recovering earlier losses, as the market weighed increases in Middle Eastern crude exports and a planned Group of Seven release of emergency diesel and crude stockpiles against supply concerns related to attacks by Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis.
Brent futures rose 26 cents, or 0.3 per cent, to settle at $100.58 a barrel, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose one cent to settle at $89.44.
Around 12 million barrels per day of crude oil and 2 million bpd of refined products — volumes needed to dampen price pressure — have left the Middle East on tankers in the last seven to 10 days, the CEO of commodity trading giant Vitol said on Tuesday.
Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman said on Tuesday that oil pumped through the East-West Pipeline, which runs to the kingdom's Red Sea export hub of Yanbu, had reached 5.8 million barrels as of Tuesday morning.

Oil price declines, however, have been limited by the possibility of further Middle East supply disruptions.
Saudi Arabia's airports in Jazan and Najran were targeted in two attacks on Monday evening, injuring three people and causing limited damage, the Saudi aviation authority said, as hostilities between the kingdom and Yemen's Iran-backed Houthis escalated.
The attacks occurred as Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces pressed a major offensive to retake territory from the Houthis, after weeks of rebel advances, with Riyadh stepping up airstrikes in support of the campaign.
Separately, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy of Ukraine said on Tuesday that the latest intelligence suggested Russia was preparing a "massive attack." 
Russia was the world's third-biggest crude oil producer behind the US and Saudi Arabia in 2025, according to US energy data. Sanctions designed to keep Russian energy out of global markets have helped support oil prices since Russia invaded Ukraine in 2022. A deal to end the Russia-Ukraine war could allow Russia to export more energy.
In the US, meanwhile, the National Hurricane Center said there was a 100 per cent chance a cyclone could form over the next seven days in the Gulf of Mexico. A storm in the US Gulf could boost oil prices by shutting oil and natural gas production and damaging other energy infrastructure.
OIL STOCKS AROUND THE WORLD
The International Energy Agency will meet next week to work out the details of a diesel stock release as market confusion grows over how many barrels Europe and the US plan to make available to address shortages and record-high prices, sources said.
The surge in diesel prices has turned the fuel, which underpins trucking, agriculture and industry, into a global political and economic concern. The wars in Iran and Ukraine have curtailed exports and damaged refineries, helping drive the rise in prices.
Under pressure from US President Donald Trump, the Group of Seven major economies agreed on Friday to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude oil from emergency reserves and pledged to refrain from imposing energy export restrictions.
With the war in Iran disrupting the flow of Middle East oil supplies, the US Energy Information Administration projected on Tuesday that world petroleum production would drop from a record 106.3 million bpd in 2025 to 101.1 million bpd in 2026, and world oil demand will drop from a record 104.4 million bpd in 2025 to 102.4 million bpd in 2026.
In 2027, however, EIA projected world oil supply and demand would rise back to record highs of 109.6 million bpd of production and 104.6 million bpd of consumption.
In the US, meanwhile, the oil market was watching for weekly storage reports from the American Petroleum Institute trade group on Tuesday and the EIA on Wednesday.
Analysts estimated energy firms added 1.7 million barrels of crude to US storage during the week ended October 2. 
If correct, it would mark the first time since August that crude stocks increased for three weeks in a row and compare with an increase of 3.7 million barrels in the same week last year and an average increase of 1.7 million barrels over the past five years (2021 to 2025). [EIA/S]

Source: Reuters

items.title: Bender: AI’s ‘Existential’ Risk Is ‘Fake’
items.summary: University of Washington professor Emily Bender argues the AI safety debate is too focused on hypothetical existential threats while overlooking harms already happening today. She points to environmental costs, disruption to workers, surveillance, misinformation and chatbot dependence. (Source: Bloomberg)

items.title: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye agree to deploy forces in Gulf
items.author: Agencies
items.summary: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye have agreed to implement the trilateral defence agreement and “provide the agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure rapid deployment” in the Gulf country ...
items.body: Pakistan, Saudi Arabia, and Turkiye have agreed to implement the trilateral defence agreement and “provide the agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure rapid deployment” in the Gulf country in the wake of Houthi attacks. The three sides had convened an emergency meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee (SPDC) of the Makkah Alliance for Defence in Riyadh on Monday to address the regional developments and threats facing Saudi Arabia, according to a joint statement. The trilateral defence agreement, signed by Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye in August, establishes a framework for collective deterrence and stipulates that an armed attack against any one of them would be regarded as an attack against all. The SPDC on Monday reviewed the outcomes of the political and military consultations preceding the meeting and approved the recommendations submitted to it. It affirmed that the Makkah agreement embodies a firm commitment to collective defence and a unified position in confronting threats. The committee “decided to move immediately to the practical implementation of the collective defence commitments and to take the necessary measures to provide the agreed military forces and capabilities and ensure their rapid deployment in the Kingdom”. “The three countries affirmed that the security of each party is an integral part of the collective security of the three countries,” the statement said. The statement did not give any details or schedule of troop deployment. It also did not specifically name the Houthis as a threat, but the development comes against the backdrop of Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. The three sides condemned in the strongest terms the attempted targeting of Makkah and Madinah, as well as the continuing attacks targeting cities and civilian and economic facilities in the Kingdom. As part of the institutional development of the alliance, the committee decided to appoint General Nauman Mahmood (Retdired) of Pakistan as the first Secretary-General for a three-year term. The SPDC meeting was held as Yemen’s Saudi-led coalition government launched a major military campaign on Sunday to recapture territory held by the Houthis. The SPDC is a key organ of the Makkah pact and comprises the foreign ministers, defence ministers and chiefs of army staff of the three members. Last month, the chiefs of defence forces and chiefs of general staff of the three countries met in Riyadh and reviewed the security situation and the threats facing Saudi Arabia. Trump faces flak fot  ‘Iran could take out LA’ remark President Donald Trump suggested to a crowd of his supporters in Nebraska that Iran could “take out” a ??major United States (US) city like Los Angeles or San Diego, drawing a swift rebuke from California’s Democratic leaders and some fellow Republicans. Trump, speaking at a political rally in the state’s farm belt on Monday, discussed American wartime economic sacrifices and said he was determined to “see a tremendous victory, because it verifies all the things we did.” “And again, remember, with the war, it’s just artificial, it’s a little bit high, it’s a small price to pay,” he told the crowd in Grand Island, Nebraska, apparently referring to rising prices of fuel, fertiliser and other products attributed to energy market disruptions from the war. “It’s a small price to pay for keeping the world safe, for keeping our country safe. They could take out a city. Let ‘em take out Los Angeles, let ‘em take out San Diego. This is a very small price to pay, and it’s going to be over with very soon,” he said.  On Tuesday, the White House dismissed criticism of the remark. “He was saying the US is fighting to STOP Iran from having the ability to take out LA and San Diego with a nuclear weapon — which they would if they had the chance,” a White House account posted on X.

items.title: OpenAI in talks with UAE funds, BlackRock for $30 billion funding round
items.author: Bloomberg
items.summary: UAE investment funds have discussed investing as much as $10 billion altogether, while OpenAI is seeking capital at a valuation of about $1.4 trillion ...
items.body: By Ed Ludlow, Rebecca Torrence, Shirin Ghaffary and Natasha Mascarenhas OpenAI is in talks with multiple investment funds from the United Arab Emirates, including Abu Dhabi-based MGX, to help anchor a $30 billion round of financing for the ChatGPT maker, according to people familiar with the matter. The funds would form a syndicate to invest in the round, one of the people said. The UAE funds have discussed putting in as much as $10 billion altogether, one person said. BlackRock Inc. is also in discussions to participate in the round alongside that syndicate, the people said. The fundraise is ongoing and the details could change, said the people, requesting anonymity to discuss private information. OpenAI and BlackRock declined to comment. Representatives for MGX did not respond to requests for comment outside normal business hours. OpenAI is looking to raise at least $30 billion in capital at a valuation of about $1.4 trillion, Bloomberg News has reported, as the firm pushes back plans for an initial public offering until at least next year, citing its focus on AI safety efforts. OpenAI most recently raised a $122 billion round in March at an $852 billion valuation, including the money. Top AI firms, including OpenAI and Anthropic PBC, have previously turned to deep-pocketed investors in the Middle East to meet their intense capital needs to develop and support cutting-edge artificial intelligence software. MGX has invested in prior OpenAI and Anthropic rounds. The investment firm raised close to $50 billion earlier this year to accelerate spending on AI infrastructure and technology, Bloomberg News has reported. OpenAI has held talks with the University of California’s endowment fund, an existing investor, about participating in the round, the people said. Existing backers Thrive Capital and Andreessen Horowitz have also discussed putting in money, the people said. Thrive declined to comment. Representatives for Andreessen and the University of California didn’t respond to requests for comment. Unlike typical venture rounds, OpenAI is presenting its $1.4 trillion pre-money valuation to investors as a set price despite not yet settling on a lead investor, the people said. Normally, investment firms submit terms for funding rounds and negotiate with the company about leading it. --With assistance from Alex Dooler

items.title: Precios de bonos del Tesoro de EEUU suben en un respiro tras desplome; subasta mejora la confianza
items.author: Gertrude Chavez-Dreyfuss
items.creator: Gertrude Chavez-Dreyfuss
items.summary: Los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos se recuperaron el martes de una ola de ventas de la víspera que llevó los retornos a largo plazo a máximos de varias décadas, porque los inversores se tomaron un respiro para evaluar los movimientos recientes a la espera de los datos de inflación de la próxima semana.
items.body:
Los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos se recuperaron el martes de una ola de ventas de la víspera que llevó los retornos a largo plazo a máximos de varias décadas, porque los inversores se tomaron un respiro para evaluar los movimientos recientes a la espera de los datos de inflación de la próxima semana.
Una sólida subasta de bonos a tres años también contribuyó al impulso alcista de los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos.
El rendimiento de referencia a 10 años cayó 4,2 puntos básicos, al 5,269%, tras alcanzar un máximo de 24 años. Los retornos a 30 años bajaron 2,2 puntos básicos, al 5,642%, tras otro máximo de 24 años del lunes.
En el extremo más corto de la curva, la rentabilidad a 2 años , sensible a las perspectivas de las tasas de interés, cayó 4,4 puntos básicos al 4,789% . La caída de los rendimientos implica que los precios de los bonos del Tesoro suben.
"Creo que los operadores están tomando aliento antes de que cambie algo en los fundamentos", dijo Will Compernolle, estratega macroeconómico de FHN Financial en Chicago. "Los operadores también están a la espera de ver cuál será el próximo gran catalizador, y no sé si vendrá de la mano del IPP (índice de precios al productor) o del IPC (índice de precios al consumidor)" .
Analistas señalaron además que los bonos del Tesoro de Estados Unidos encontraron apoyo tras un repunte similar en los bonos de la zona del euro, especialmente los franceses.
Los costos de financiación de Francia se han disparado en las últimas semanas y el diferencial de rendimiento respecto a Alemania se amplió el viernes hasta su nivel más alto desde la crisis de la deuda de la zona euro en 2011. El repunte de las tasas ocurrió en un contexto de preocupación por el deterioro de la situación fiscal del país antes de las elecciones presidenciales del próximo año.
La curva de rendimientos se aplanó el martes, y el diferencial entre las tasas a dos y 10 años se reducía a 47,8 puntos básicos desde los 48,9 puntos básicos del lunes. La curva había alcanzado el lunes su nivel más pronunciado en siete semanas, después de que los retornos a largo plazo subieron con mayor intensidad que los de plazo más corto.

items.author: ロイター
items.creator: ロイター
items.summary: [モスクワ　６日　ロイター] -
items.body:
[モスクワ　６日　ロイター] - ロシアのウシャコフ大統領補佐官は６日、中国で１１月に開かれるアジア太平洋経済協力会議（ＡＰＥＣ）首脳会議に合わせ、プーチン大統領、トランプ米大統領、中国の習近平国家主席による３者会談が実現する可能性について、ロシアとして関心を持っていると述べた。

ウシャコフ氏は、この構想は初期段階にあり、詳細はまだ調整されていないとした上で、ＡＰＥＣ首脳会議の議長国を務める中国が今後議題を提示するとし、３カ国首脳による会談の機会が設けられる可能性があるとの見方を示した。

ＡＰＥＣ首脳会議は１１月１８─１９日に開かれる。

ウシャコフ氏はこのほか、イランのペゼシュキアン大統領が９日にトルクメニスタンで開かれる旧ソ連諸国首脳会議に出席し、その際にプーチン大統領と会談すると明らかにした。

FAST

LONDON/SEOUL, Oct 6 : Russia imported more than 176,000 tons of petroleum products from South Korean ports in July and August, easing the impact of a fuel crisis caused by Ukrainian drone strikes on Russian oil refineries, Ukraine's top sanctions official said on Tuesday.
The supplies from South Korea made up 31 per cent of Russian fuel imports in August, according to the official, Vladyslav Vlasiuk, citing what he said were reports that tankers, including ones under Western sanctions, were used for the deliveries.
"These shipments began precisely when Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil refineries were reducing processing volumes and creating a fuel shortage within Russia," Vlasiuk, presidential commissioner for Ukrainian sanctions policy, wrote on Facebook.
His comments come amid a diplomatic row between Seoul and Kyiv that erupted last month when President Volodymyr Zelenskiy announced the transfer of two North Korean prisoners of war to South Korea, a step that Seoul says was meant to stay secret.
